setup: The 139 golden-set cases without line breaks, voiced with macOS say (build_polish_corpus.py). Express: whole-utterance decode, no Word Boost (the golden set has no dictionary). Turbo: the app's live path. Both transcripts go through the app's rule stage (DisfluencyCleaner, then SpokenFormattingFormatter; ORTTAAI_ASR_EVAL_RULES=1), then polish_eval.py --transcripts with the production prompt, sanitizer and gemma4:e2b (Ollama, MLX runner). Release build, Apple M5 Max.

clean_text_ceiling.note: Golden raw text through polish, no speech engine

verdict: Polish needs no change for Express: it lifts Express output by 4.3 points against 2.9 for turbo. End to end Express trails turbo by 5.8 points, missing the 2-point target, and the whole gap comes from the transcripts (7.2 points before polish).
notes: 14 cases pass only with turbo and 6 only with Express. The turbo-only ones are mishearings without a dictionary (Adayemi, localhost, writes, Adebayo), contractions Mini writes out in full (we're -> we are, 3 cases), and spellings the strict checks count as lost words (3 pm vs 3pm, 4,471 for an account number, the 20th of July).
Names would normally go through Word Boost with the user's dictionary; this run has none, so it understates Express on proper nouns.

The golden checks are token-strict, which is why both engines sit far below the 89.9% clean-text ceiling: 3.2% vs 3.2 percent or 15,000 vs fifteen thousand fail a case even when the meaning is identical.
The clean-text ceiling was 92.8% in eval_results.json (2026-07-27) on an older Ollama runtime; the same model scores 90.1% on all 152 cases here, with a p50 of 65 ms instead of 1.16 s.
